question: Atoms of different elements with different ___________ numbers but the same ______ number are known as isobars.
solution:
The correct answer is __**atomic, mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobars** are defined as atoms of different **chemical elements** that have the same **mass number** (total number of **nucleons**) but different **atomic numbers** (number of **protons**).
 
• The term **isobar** was suggested by **Alfred Walter Stewart** in the year **1918**. It is derived from the Greek words "isos" meaning equal and "baros" meaning weight.
 
• Because **isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they occupy different positions in the **periodic table** and possess different **chemical properties**.
 
• Examples of **isobars** include **Argon** (**atomic number 18**), **Potassium** (**atomic number 19**), and **Calcium** (**atomic number 20**), all of which can have a **mass number** of **40**.
 
• Since their **mass numbers** are the same, their **physical properties**, which depend on the mass of the atom, may be quite similar, though their **electronic configurations** differ significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• It represents the number of **protons** found in the **nucleus** of every atom of that element.
 
• It uniquely identifies a **chemical element**. For instance, any atom with **6 protons** is an atom of **Carbon**.
 
 
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• It is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in an atomic nucleus.
 
• While the **atomic number** is usually constant for an element, the **mass number** can vary, leading to the formation of **isotopes**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the **same element** that have the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (1 proton, 0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 proton, 1 neutron), and **Tritium** (1 proton, 2 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Isotones:**
 
 
• These are atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons** but different **atomic numbers** and **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **Carbon-14** (6 protons, 8 neutrons) and **Oxygen-16** (8 protons, 8 neutrons) are **isotones**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nucleons** is the collective term used for **protons** and **neutrons**, both of which reside in the **nucleus** of an atom.
 
• The number of **electrons** in a neutral atom is equal to its **atomic number**. Since **isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they have a different number of **electrons**, leading to their distinct **chemical reactivity**.
 
• In nuclear physics, **isobars** are relevant in **beta decay**. In **beta minus decay**, a **neutron** turns into a **proton**, meaning the **atomic number** increases by 1 while the **mass number** remains constant, effectively creating an **isobar** of the parent atom.
 
• The **atomic mass** of an element is the weighted average of the masses of its naturally occurring **isotopes** and is measured in **atomic mass units (amu)**.
</ul
